machine: steward runner, 4 cores, no GPU (SwiftShader), headless Chromium

why_the_ground_first.tool: spatial-batch.js and terrain.js timed in place on the source tree (a throwaway probe, not committed), mobile 390x780 touch, detail light

ground_build_ms.note: cumulative from createTerrain's ground load: GLB load, then conform, then tileGround, then every tile partitioned on the job pool

why_the_ground_first.reading: At the phone profile the ground's load, conform, tile and partition come to 3.0 s of the terrain phase's 8.8 s (T-2677's before reading), and the ground is 222 of the page's 231 spatial-batch calls. So T-2678 was split: the ground in Node (this), the page uploading it (T-2693), and the town's other nine calls (T-2694).

file.note: A second gzip pass gains 0.7 %, against frontage's 35 %: the ground does not repeat itself the way the timber does. The index states each tile's attributes once and each piece only as offsets; with a name, type and sha256 per array it was 9.5 MB.

parity.note: each of the live page's ground tiles (BatchedMesh geometry: _confidence, position, normal and index), by sha256, against the Node build's pieces batched with spatial-batch.js's own batchPieces

reading: The 1835 ground, cut in Node by the page's own functions, is byte-equal to what the page draws: 669 of 669 attributes over 223 tiles and 9,405 pieces, zero page errors. Built in about 0.65 s on this runner. Shipped, it would cost about 10.6 MB gzipped on top of the 30.5 MB ground GLB the page fetches today, unless T-2693 serves it in the GLB's place.
